- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- After sharp sentiment spikes (≥0.67 followed by +0.33 or higher sentiment change), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) and news volume drops below 2.0, model overcorrects downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to avoid mean reversion trap.
- When sentiment change is negative and news volume is stable, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for lagged sentiment effect.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., >5% gap), apply “mean reversion” rule: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- If sentiment is volatile (±0.33 change) and news volume is high, model is prone to overfitting; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent 7-day high.
